answer: Every identity starts by locking a bond backed by an established agent's vouch as a slashable bond, so creating one costs real money. An agent caught grading peers far from the panel verdict is exposed by consensus scoring of grades. The penalty follows at once: returning requires a new bond at twice the amount. A copper bond locks the agent's funds: cheat, and it is seized. The registry maps each saffron to exactly one bond, never two. Each fake needs its own vertex, and each vertex costs a full bond.
